questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.answer: The nature and the fact that its an english speaking country

Additional comments:

questions.answer: not easy at all, there is lack of information from my univerity and U of A

questions.answer: I was lucky that my friend had been there the semester before me, so i just texted him

Additional comments
questions.answer: not much information and assistance

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: bad dorms for expensive prices. i stayed at international house which costed 1400 cad/month.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was expensive meal plans, i just cooked at the shared kithcen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: you have to bring everything, there is not even kitchen stuff, blankets ect. not even washing liquid at the shared kitchens. Also have in mind that the walls are very thin and some students doesn't respect the quiet hours. when you try to complain about it, the housing facilities does not help you at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not possible to find much information about the different courses and examination methods... you figure it out when you have first class. but its good that you are able to switch courses the first 1-2 weeks after the semester begins

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just use the portal on bear tracks to find the available courses, and then registre

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not much help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I just took the courses that was available at the time i entered the portal.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: be ready when the courses for the semester gets released for registre. If you don't get the courses you want, then select the ones you can, and look frequently to see if new spots opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was a bit lower than the level in Denmark. I did not find the courses very hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, we only have 100% final grade exams in denmark. At U of A the examination varies. Some courses even have participation grading.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, canadians are like danes, but easier to talk to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just talk to people, canadians loves to chat.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: being use to easy (and safe) public transportation and come to a coutry where everyone have cars. You feel paralised if you dont have a car.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Go to the saloon, cook country and get the cowboy experience. 

and in general, canadians are really nice people so just talk with strangers, they love it.

questions.answer:
Eventhough its expensive and not that good - live at campus. 
- because its where you meet people 
- Edmonton is cold ant not a good city if you dont own a car. 

travel as much as possible

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: travelling - travel as much as possible. There is not much to do in Edmonton

questions.answer: understanding common law system and the perspective of indigenous law - therefore i would recomend not taking any domestic law courses if possible.
